WELCOME TO ALAMINOS CITY
Alaminos City is the home and main gateway of Hundred Islands National Park. The city combines island-hopping, coastal

For visitors, Lucap is the key area because Lucap Wharf is the departure point for Hundred Islands. Poblacion provides
access to the city center, while coastal areas such as Bolo and Telbang offer beach and resort options.

profile: Bolinao is a municipality in western Pangasinan facing the West Philippine Sea. The Province of Pangasinan describes it as a major beach and nature destination, with Patar Beach, Balingasay River, giant-clam conservation, and the historic Cape Bolinao Lighthouse among its attractions. The town also has a long fishing tradition, reflected in the annual Mangunguna Festival. A signature local food is binungey, sticky rice cooked inside bamboo over charcoal or wood fire. Best for  Waterfalls: Bolinao Falls 1, 2 and 3, with swimming, pools, and locally offered rafting/kayaking activities.  Beach trips: Patar Beach, rock formations, sunset viewing, and coastal photography.  Nature: Balingasay River cruises, Enchanted Cave, and giant-clam/ecotourism experiences.  Heritage: Cape Bolinao Lighthouse and Saint James the Great Parish Church.  Food: Binungey, seafood, grilled dishes, and Pangasinan delicacies.

attractions.name: Patar White Sand Beach
attractions.description: Bolinao's signature beach destination, known for its light-colored sand, coconut-lined coast, rock formations, and sunsets. It is one of the municipality's most popular stops for swimming, relaxing, and photography.

attractions.name: Cape Bolinao Lighthouse
attractions.description: A historic lighthouse built in 1905 on Cape Bolinao. It stands on a rocky coastal promontory and is one of the town's best-known heritage and photography landmarks.

attractions.name: Enchanted Cave
attractions.description: A natural limestone cave with a clear freshwater pool. The cave is a popular swimming and nature attraction and can be paired with Patar Beach and the lighthouse on the same day.

attractions.name: Balingasay River
attractions.description: A mangrove-lined river and ecotourism attraction associated with boat cruises and floating dining. The Province of Pangasinan highlights it as the cleanest river in Region 1 and one of Bolinao's key natural assets.

attractions.name: Saint James the Great Parish Church
attractions.description: A historic church in Barangay Germinal. Philippine government tourism reporting identifies it as a major heritage and Holy Week destination, with black coral-stone construction and a tall bell tower.
aliases: St. James the Great Parish Church

attractions.name: Bolinao Falls 1–3
attractions.description: The municipality's famous inland waterfall cluster in Barangay Samang Norte. The three numbered falls offer different swimming pools and visitor experiences and are commonly visited together.

attractions.name: Giant Clam / Marine Conservation Experience

attractions.name: Old Rock / Rock Formations
attractions.description: The coastal rock formations around Patar provide scenic viewpoints and are popular for photography, especially around golden hour.

attractions.name: Patar-area Caves and Nature Attractions
attractions.description: Bolinao's limestone landscape supports several cave and nature attractions. Access can vary by site; use established guides and current local tourism information.

activities.name: Waterfall-hopping

activities.name: Beach day at Patar

activities.name: Sunset photography

activities.name: Balingasay River cruise
activities.description: Take a river cruise or floating-cottage experience when operating. River dining and mangrove scenery make this a slower alternative to the beach.

activities.name: Cave swimming

activities.description: Learn about Bolinao's giant-clam conservation work through an operating local tour or facility.

activities.name: Heritage tour
activities.description: Visit Saint James the Great Parish Church and Cape Bolinao Lighthouse for a combination of religious and maritime history.

practical_notes:  Waterfall safety: Confirm current swimming conditions and local rules. Wear a life jacket when required, especially in deep pools, and avoid unapproved cliff jumps.  Water activities: Banana boats, jet skis, kayaking, and island-hopping depend on weather, sea conditions, and current operators.  Swimming hours: Recent Philippine government tourism guidance reported swimming at Bolinao attractions as allowed from 6:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.; verify current local rules before entering the water.  Falls fees: Online reports show different fee structures over time. Treat posted online prices as estimates and confirm the current entrance, parking, cottage, raft, kayak, and life-jacket fees locally.  Best waterfall timing: Starting early helps avoid the strongest midday heat and allows more time for all three falls.  Beach conditions: Sea conditions and weather can affect swimming and boat activities. Follow local advisories.  Local transport: Tricycles, private vehicles, and hired local transport are practical for linking Patar, Samang Norte, town, and river areas.  Respect the environment: Keep plastic and food waste out of beaches, caves, rivers, and waterfall areas; do not damage coral, limestone, mangroves, or marine life.
access_note: Confirm current swimming conditions and local rules. Use designated swimming areas, wear a life jacket where required, and do not jump from unapproved heights. Water activities and marine tours depend on current operators, weather and access.

1. BOLINAO AT A GLANCE
Bolinao is a municipality in western Pangasinan facing the West Philippine Sea. The Province of Pangasinan describes it
as a major beach and nature destination, with Patar Beach, Balingasay River, giant-clam conservation, and the historic
Cape Bolinao Lighthouse among its attractions.
The town also has a long fishing tradition, reflected in the annual Mangunguna Festival. A signature local food is
binungey, sticky rice cooked inside bamboo over charcoal or wood fire.
Best for
 Waterfalls: Bolinao Falls 1, 2 and 3, with swimming, pools, and locally offered rafting/kayaking activities.
 Beach trips: Patar Beach, rock formations, sunset viewing, and coastal photography.
 Nature: Balingasay River cruises, Enchanted Cave, and giant-clam/ecotourism experiences.
 Heritage: Cape Bolinao Lighthouse and Saint James the Great Parish Church.
 Food: Binungey, seafood, grilled dishes, and Pangasinan delicacies.
2. TOP PLACES TO VISIT
1. Patar White Sand Beach
Bolinao's signature beach destination, known for its light-colored sand, coconut-lined coast, rock formations, and sunsets.
It is one of the municipality's most popular stops for swimming, relaxing, and photography.
2. Cape Bolinao Lighthouse
A historic lighthouse built in 1905 on Cape Bolinao. It stands on a rocky coastal promontory and is one of the town's
best-known heritage and photography landmarks.
3. Enchanted Cave
A natural limestone cave with a clear freshwater pool. The cave is a popular swimming and nature attraction and can be
paired with Patar Beach and the lighthouse on the same day.
4. Balingasay River
A mangrove-lined river and ecotourism attraction associated with boat cruises and floating dining. The Province of
Pangasinan highlights it as the cleanest river in Region 1 and one of Bolinao's key natural assets.
5. Saint James the Great Parish Church
A historic church in Barangay Germinal. Philippine government tourism reporting identifies it as a major heritage and Holy
Week destination, with black coral-stone construction and a tall bell tower.
6. Bolinao Falls 1–3
The municipality's famous inland waterfall cluster in Barangay Samang Norte. The three numbered falls offer different
swimming pools and visitor experiences and are commonly visited together.
7. Giant Clam / Marine Conservation Experience
Bolinao is associated with giant-clam conservation and marine research. Visitor access and tour arrangements can vary,
so confirm the currently operating facility or tour provider before travel.
8. Old Rock / Rock Formations
The coastal rock formations around Patar provide scenic viewpoints and are popular for photography, especially around
golden hour.

9. Patar-area Caves and Nature Attractions
Bolinao's limestone landscape supports several cave and nature attractions. Access can vary by site; use established
guides and current local tourism information.
3. FAMOUS FALLS — BOLINAO FALLS 1, 2 & 3
Bolinao Falls is a cluster of three well-known freshwater swimming stops in Barangay Samang Norte. Current local
sources describe Falls 1, 2 and 3 as connected by the same general stream system and close enough to visit in one
outing. Conditions, entrance fees, life-jacket rules, cottages, and operating arrangements can change, so confirm locally
on the day.
Bolinao Falls 1
The tallest and most dramatic of the three. It has a deep catch basin and is associated with swimming, bamboo-raft/kayak
activities, and a jump platform. Deep water and slippery rocks make life-jacket use and conservative swimming important.
Bolinao Falls 2
A more relaxed waterfall stop with a broader swimming area. The Falls 2 area is also associated with a shallow
spring-falls section and rock pools, giving visitors more options for wading and swimming.
Bolinao Falls 3
Known for a wide pool, surrounding greenery, rock formations, and locally offered bamboo-raft activities. It also has
shallower areas that can suit visitors who prefer relaxed swimming, subject to current water conditions.

Safety: Water depth, currents, rocks, and local rules can change. Use designated swimming areas, follow caretakers'
instructions, wear a life jacket where required, and do not jump from unapproved heights.
4. THINGS TO DO IN BOLINAO
1. Waterfall-hopping
Spend a half-day or full morning visiting Falls 1, 2 and 3. Start early to allow time for travel, swimming, and changing local
conditions.
2. Beach day at Patar
Swim, relax, photograph the coastline, explore rock formations, and stay for sunset.
3. Sunset photography
Combine Patar Beach and the coastal rock formations with Cape Bolinao Lighthouse for a dedicated golden-hour photo
circuit.
4. Balingasay River cruise
Take a river cruise or floating-cottage experience when operating. River dining and mangrove scenery make this a slower
alternative to the beach.

5. Cave swimming
Swim in the freshwater pool at Enchanted Cave and explore the surrounding limestone landscape.
6. Island / coastal activities
Depending on current local operators and sea conditions, activities can include island hopping, kayaking, banana boat
rides, and jet skiing.
7. Giant-clam and marine tourism
Learn about Bolinao's giant-clam conservation work through an operating local tour or facility.
8. Heritage tour
Visit Saint James the Great Parish Church and Cape Bolinao Lighthouse for a combination of religious and maritime
history.
9. Seafood food trip
Try locally prepared seafood, grilled dishes, and river-side dining in Bolinao.
10. Try binungey
Taste the municipality's signature bamboo-cooked sticky-rice delicacy.
11. Camping / beach stay
Bolinao has numerous beach resorts, vacation houses, and camping-style accommodations, especially around Patar.
12. Mangunguna Festival
If your visit coincides with the annual fisherman-themed festival, check the municipal calendar for the current year's public

 coral, limestone, mangroves, or marine life.

profile: Lingayen was founded in 1614 and became the capital of Pangasinan. Its history includes the World War II landing in Lingayen Gulf and a strong civic and cultural landscape around the provincial Capitol complex. Today, the town combines coastal recreation, heritage sites, food tourism, and local industry. The Municipality of Lingayen identifies bagoong as its One Town, One Product (OTOP). Its coastal setting, the Agno River, and an 11.5-kilometer coastline support fisheries and other aquatic resources, while local tourism highlights heritage buildings, the Baywalk, and the Limahong Channel. Best for  Heritage: Casa Real, the Capitol complex, Sison Auditorium, churches, and WWII memorial sites.  Coastal leisure: Lingayen Beach and Baywalk, sunsets, walks, and photo stops.  Food tourism: Lingayen bagoong, bagoong-based dishes, sundot-kulangot, kalamay, and local seafood.  Ecotourism: Limahong Channel, its tourism center, and the nearby bike/ecotourism area.

attractions.name: Lingayen Beach & Baywalk
attractions.description: A scenic coastal public area and one of Lingayen's signature visitor stops. The municipal tourism page describes it as a tranquil gathering and pictorial site. Ideal for walking, sunset viewing, casual recreation, and photography.

attractions.name: Casa Real / Provincial Museum
attractions.description: A restored national historical landmark and former provincial seat of government. The building dates to the Spanish period and now houses the provincial museum, making it a key stop for Lingayen and Pangasinan history.

attractions.name: Pangasinan Provincial Capitol
attractions.description: The provincial government center and a major architectural landmark in Lingayen. Include the Capitol complex in a heritage walk, while observing public-access rules for government offices.

attractions.name: Urduja House
attractions.description: The official residence of the Governor of Pangasinan, located in the Capitol complex. Best treated as an exterior/heritage viewing stop unless an authorized visit or event provides access.

attractions.name: Sison Auditorium
attractions.description: A major cultural venue in the provincial capital used for social and cultural events. Check the current event schedule if you want to see a performance or public program.

attractions.name: Limahong Channel & Tourism Center
attractions.description: A historical and ecotourism site associated with Limahong's 1574 escape route. Municipal plans and tourism materials highlight the channel as a place for history, nature, and recreational activities.

attractions.name: Veterans Memorial Park
attractions.description: An open-air WWII heritage site with relics and memorabilia, including the MacArthur Landing Marker. It provides context for the historic Lingayen Gulf landing.

attractions.name: Epiphany of Our Lord Parish
attractions.description: A historic Roman Catholic church formerly known as the Three Kings Parish and identified by the municipal tourism office as one of the country's older Catholic churches.

This guide covers Lingayen, Pangasinan only. Attractions, activities, hotels, resorts, and food stops
listed here are within the Municipality of Lingayen. Neighboring municipalities and cities are intentionally
excluded.
Lingayen is the capital municipality of Pangasinan and a coastal heritage destination shaped by government, history, the
Lingayen Gulf, and its long-standing bagoong-making industry.
Guide basis: official municipal/provincial tourism information plus current local business listings checked in September 2026.

Lingayen Tourism Guide    Page 2
1. LINGAYEN AT A GLANCE
Lingayen was founded in 1614 and became the capital of Pangasinan. Its history includes the World War II landing in
Lingayen Gulf and a strong civic and cultural landscape around the provincial Capitol complex. Today, the town combines
coastal recreation, heritage sites, food tourism, and local industry.
The Municipality of Lingayen identifies bagoong as its One Town, One Product (OTOP). Its coastal setting, the Agno
River, and an 11.5-kilometer coastline support fisheries and other aquatic resources, while local tourism highlights
heritage buildings, the Baywalk, and the Limahong Channel.
Best for
 Heritage: Casa Real, the Capitol complex, Sison Auditorium, churches, and WWII memorial sites.
 Coastal leisure: Lingayen Beach and Baywalk, sunsets, walks, and photo stops.
 Food tourism: Lingayen bagoong, bagoong-based dishes, sundot-kulangot, kalamay, and local seafood.
 Ecotourism: Limahong Channel, its tourism center, and the nearby bike/ecotourism area.
2. PLACES TO VISIT
1. Lingayen Beach & Baywalk
A scenic coastal public area and one of Lingayen's signature visitor stops. The municipal tourism page describes it as a
tranquil gathering and pictorial site. Ideal for walking, sunset viewing, casual recreation, and photography.
2. Casa Real / Provincial Museum
A restored national historical landmark and former provincial seat of government. The building dates to the Spanish period
and now houses the provincial museum, making it a key stop for Lingayen and Pangasinan history.
3. Pangasinan Provincial Capitol
The provincial government center and a major architectural landmark in Lingayen. Include the Capitol complex in a
heritage walk, while observing public-access rules for government offices.
4. Urduja House
The official residence of the Governor of Pangasinan, located in the Capitol complex. Best treated as an exterior/heritage
viewing stop unless an authorized visit or event provides access.
5. Sison Auditorium
A major cultural venue in the provincial capital used for social and cultural events. Check the current event schedule if you
want to see a performance or public program.
6. Limahong Channel & Tourism Center
A historical and ecotourism site associated with Limahong's 1574 escape route. Municipal plans and tourism materials
highlight the channel as a place for history, nature, and recreational activities.
7. Veterans Memorial Park
An open-air WWII heritage site with relics and memorabilia, including the MacArthur Landing Marker. It provides context
for the historic Lingayen Gulf landing.
8. Epiphany of Our Lord Parish
A historic Roman Catholic church formerly known as the Three Kings Parish and identified by the municipal tourism office
as one of the country's older Catholic churches.

9. Fidel V. Ramos Ancestral Home
The well-preserved ancestral home of former Philippine President Fidel V. Ramos, identified by the Province of
Pangasinan as a Lingayen heritage attraction. Observe any private-property or access restrictions.
10. Lingayen Town Plaza
A central civic landmark in the town proper, located in front of the Municipal Hall. It works well as a short stop when
combining the town center with nearby heritage sites.
11. Narciso Ramos Sports & Civic Center
A venue for local, regional, and national sports and civic activities. Check event schedules when planning a visit.
12. Colegio del Santissimo Rosario Ruins
Remains associated with the former girls' school run by Dominican sisters. The municipal tourism office notes that the site
is now part of private property, so viewing should respect access restrictions.

3. THINGS TO DO
1. Heritage walking tour
Start around the Town Plaza and municipal center, then continue toward Casa Real, the Capitol complex, Sison
Auditorium, and other nearby heritage landmarks.
2. Beach and Baywalk afternoon
Spend a relaxed afternoon along Lingayen Beach and Baywalk. Pair a coastal walk with sunset photography and a local
meal.
3. Museum and history stop
Visit Casa Real/Provincial Museum to deepen the historical context before seeing the WWII memorial sites.
4. Limahong Channel exploration
Visit the Limahong Channel Tourism Center and surrounding ecotourism area. Depending on current operations, activities
may include cycling and nature-oriented recreation.
5. Bagoong food trip
Try Lingayen bagoong as a condiment or in prepared dishes, and look for local manufacturers or food showcases when
available.
6. Local delicacy tasting
Try sundot-kulangot and kalamay, both highlighted by the municipal tourism office during its 2026 food showcase.
7. Seafood and coastal dining
Look for local seafood and Filipino dishes in Lingayen's town-center and coastal dining areas.
8. Festival experience
If visiting during the annual Bagoong Festival, join public food, cultural, cooking, and street-dance activities. The 2026
celebration ran March 18–20.
9. Photography circuit
Combine the Baywalk, Town Plaza, heritage buildings, Capitol grounds, and WWII markers for a full-day photo route.
4. LINGAYEN BAGOONG FESTIVAL
Bagoong is Lingayen's OTOP and a defining part of its food identity. The municipality has celebrated the Bagoong
Festival since 2011. The 2026 edition ran March 18–20 and included food showcases, a cooking competition, cultural
activities, and street-dancing events.
The 2026 Taway-Taway Food Showcase highlighted sundot-kulangot, kalamay, bagoong fried rice, and bagoong
longganisa. A 2026 Philippine Information Agency report also documented a cooking competition centered on bagoong
and alamang.
Planning tip: Festival dates and road closures can change each year. Check the Municipality of Lingayen's current
announcements before traveling.

3. THINGS TO DO

subject to change.
2. Light candles and visit the devotional areas

pace.

Add the Pugaro site to a pilgrimage itinerary and allow extra time for the rural approach.

WELCOME TO SAN CARLOS CITY
San Carlos City was historically known as Binalatongan and was associated with Caboloan. The present city was created
from the former municipality of San Carlos under Republic Act No. 4487 in 1965. The Province of Pangasinan describes
San Carlos as a major trading center for bamboo and a leading producer of carabao mangoes.
The city government presents San Carlos as an agro-industrial, commercial, educational, and tourism center. Its tourism
character is centered on heritage, agriculture, mangoes, bamboo crafts, food, parks, and inland resorts.
PLACES TO VISIT & ATTRACTIONS

San Carlos City's major historic church. The city tourism site states that the church's history dates to the arrival of the

repeated earthquake damage and reconstruction. It was declared a Minor Basilica in 2022 and solemnly proclaimed in

Bamboo Craft & Furniture Areas

The Mango-Bamboo Festival is San Carlos City's signature celebration. The city tourism site says it is held annually around

profile: Urdaneta City is a component city of Pangasinan with 34 barangays. Its strategic location has made it a major trading and agricultural hub.  A city-only guide to Urdaneta City, Pangasinan
Urdaneta is a commercial and agricultural center in Pangasinan, known for its public market, rice fields,
cultural sites, parks, resorts, and locally developed food products.
Prepared using current City Government of Urdaneta information and current local listings.

Urdaneta City Tourism Guide    Page 2
WELCOME TO URDANETA CITY
Urdaneta City is a component city of Pangasinan with 34 barangays. Its strategic location has made it a major trading and
agricultural hub. The provincial government identifies rice, vegetables, and noodles among products associated with the
city, while the City Government highlights its markets, rice fields, cultural spaces, parks, and resorts as visitor experiences.
Unlike Pangasinan's coastal destinations, Urdaneta's tourism character is centered on city life, agriculture, food, culture,
faith, commerce, and inland leisure.
PLACES TO VISIT & ATTRACTIONS
Museo de Urdaneta / Urdaneta City New Museum
A city heritage and cultural stop. The museum is located on Alexander Street and is listed among Urdaneta's attractions by
the Provincial Government. Current local listings identify the New Museum as a tourist attraction.
Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception
A major religious landmark in the city center and a continuation of Urdaneta's long church history. The City Government
specifically highlights Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception as part of the city's heritage.
Urdaneta City People's Park
An urban green space for walking, relaxation, recreation, and community activities. The City Government describes it as a
tranquil urban oasis with greenery and ponds.
Urdaneta City Cultural Center
A venue for cultural and artistic events and community gatherings. It provides a place to experience local programs and
cultural activities when events are scheduled.
Urdaneta City Public Market
A lively market where visitors can see the city's trading culture, buy fresh produce, discover local delicacies, and experience
everyday Urdaneta life.
Urdaneta Farmer's Market / Agricultural Trading Areas
A good place to explore the city's agricultural identity through locally produced vegetables, rice, fruits, and other farm
products.
Rice Fields of Urdaneta
Scenic agricultural landscapes that reflect the city's farming heritage. The City Government specifically features Urdaneta's
rice fields as a tourism experience.
Cattle Market / Livestock Area
A distinctive part of Urdaneta's agricultural and trading character. The City Government features its cattle market/farm
among places to discover.
Cabaruan
Cabaruan is identified by the Provincial Government as one of Urdaneta City's attractions. It is also one of the city's 34
barangays.
Sugcong
Sugcong is identified by the Provincial Government as an attraction in Urdaneta City and is one of the city's barangays.
Oltama Rolling Hills
A countryside landscape attraction identified by the Provincial Government as one of Urdaneta City's notable attractions.
ACTIVITIES TO DO
City heritage tour
Visit the museum, cathedral, cultural spaces, and other central-city landmarks.

Urdaneta City Tourism Guide    Page 3
Market and food tour
Explore the public market, local stalls, street food, and products made by Urdaneta communities.
Agricultural sightseeing
Take a countryside drive or walk through appropriate public areas near the city's rice-growing landscapes.
Photography at rice fields
Capture rural scenery, especially during planting or harvest seasons, while respecting private farmland.
Relax at People's Park
Spend time walking, taking photographs, or enjoying the park's landscaped environment.
Resort day
Book a day-use or overnight stay at an Urdaneta City resort for swimming and leisure.
Food tourism
Seek out Urdaneta-made products such as tinapang manok, smoked or marinated bangus, rabbit-meat products, native
delicacies, and other barangay products.
Festival and cultural events
Check the City Government's announcements for Pinaglakwan Festival, Christmas Festival, cultural performances, and
other scheduled events.

LOCAL FOODS & PRODUCTS TO TRY
 Food / Product
What to try
Tinapang Manok
Smoked chicken is one of Urdaneta's recognized local food products. The City Tourism Office has promoted it as a signature product of Barangay Bayaoas.
Tinapa / Smoked Fish
Urdaneta has a long-established tinapa industry in Barangay Bayaoas. Look for smoked fish and related products in local markets.
Smoked & Marinated Bangus
A product featured in Urdaneta's local food festivals and barangay product showcases.
Rabbit Meat Products
Urdaneta food producers have developed rabbit-meat products including longganisa, hotdogs, embutido, and lechon. Availability can vary.
Kamoteng Biko
A native rice-and-root-crop delicacy featured in Urdaneta's Tourism Month food activities.
Hopia
A local product featured in the city's One Barangay, One Product food exhibition.
Peanut Butter
Another product showcased by Urdaneta communities during the city's food tourism activities.
Pansit / Local Noodles
Urdaneta is identified by the Provincial Government as a producer of noodles, and local food exhibitions have included pansit.
Buko Pie
Featured among Urdaneta's locally showcased delicacies.
Papaya Pickles
A local product featured in the city's food exhibition and barangay product showcase.

RESTAURANTS & FOOD STOPS
For visitors who want named dining stops inside Urdaneta City, current local listings include Matutina–Gerry's Seafood
House in Nancayasan, BountiFULL restaurant on MacArthur Highway, Primo's Bistro & Café at Wheels & Wonders Center,
Janchi Korean Restaurant in Nancayasan, Kuya J at SM City Urdaneta Central, and local eateries around the public market.
For a distinctly Urdaneta food experience, prioritize the public market and local products described above.
SAMPLE 1-DAY URDANETA CITY ITINERARY
 Time
Plan
Morning
Start at the Urdaneta City Public Market → breakfast and local-product shopping → visit the Cathedral of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception.
Late morning
Visit Museo de Urdaneta / Urdaneta City New Museum → continue to nearby central-city cultural sites.
Lunch
Try local food, including smoked products or other Urdaneta-made specialties.
Afternoon
People's Park → Urdaneta City Cultural Center if an event is scheduled → countryside drive toward rice-field areas.
Late afternoon
Visit an Urdaneta City resort for swimming/leisure, or explore a suitable rural viewpoint around Oltama/Cabaruan/Sugcong.
Evening
Dinner at a local restaurant → evening market/food stop if operating → return to your Urdaneta City hotel.
FESTIVALS & EVENTS
Pinaglakwan Festival is identified by the City Government as a celebration of Urdaneta's agricultural heritage and the work
of its farmers, with activities such as parades, street dancing, and cultural performances. The city also holds seasonal and
community events such as its Christmas Festival and farmer's market activities. Event dates can change from year to year,
so check the City Government's current announcements before planning around a festival.

PRACTICAL TRAVEL NOTES
Getting around
Urdaneta is a busy inland commercial city. Tricycles and road-based transport are useful for moving between the city center,
barangays, markets, and resorts.
Best for
Food trips, market exploration, cultural visits, inland countryside scenery, family resort stays, and experiencing everyday city
life.
Respect private farmland
Rice fields and agricultural areas are often working/private properties. Stay on public roads or obtain permission before
entering fields.
Check event schedules
Cultural-center programs, festivals, market events, and special tourism activities are scheduled periodically.
Confirm businesses
Hotel amenities, restaurant hours, and resort access can change. Contact establishments before traveling.
